subject.title: Hard-delete or runtimeId migration needed for @apify/apify-openclaw-plugin

question: Should an authorized ClawHub admin apply the runtimeId repair to the production Apify package, or choose a hard-delete/other migration path after verifying package ownership and collisions?
rationale: This changes production package identity for an executable plugin, so source code cannot safely decide the data mutation without maintainer authority and security-boundary checks.

options.title: Run guarded runtimeId repair
options.body: Use the admin dry-run/apply flow after verifying Apify ownership, current package state, and no active `apify-openclaw-plugin` runtimeId collision.

options.title: Use destructive migration
options.body: Hard-delete, retire, or otherwise migrate the entry only if the guarded runtimeId repair cannot preserve the intended package identity safely.

options.title: Wait for stronger identity proof
options.body: Keep the package blocked until maintainers have enough publisher or organization verification to mutate the production package record.

recommendation.title: Run guarded runtimeId repair
recommendation.body: Use the admin dry-run/apply flow after verifying Apify ownership, current package state, and no active `apify-openclaw-plugin` runtimeId collision.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged operator repair flows and handled the analogous OpenViking package repair path.
